messages.content:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: The Landlord may increase the rent by up to the guideline amount once in any 12-month period by giving the Tenant 30 days' written notice.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
**No. The clause is not enforceable as written, because it allows only 30 days' notice of a rent increase.**

**The notice period is the defect.** Section 116(1) of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 requires a landlord to give the tenant **at least 90 days' written notice** of a rent increase. Section 116(3) requires the notice to be in the approved form, which is LTB Form N1. Section 116(4) states that an increase made without proper notice is **void**. A clause permitting an increase on 30 days' notice, in any written form, falls short of that minimum.

**The tenant cannot agree to less.** Under section 3(1), the Act applies despite any agreement to the contrary. Under section 4, a provision in a tenancy agreement that is inconsistent with the Act is void. Signing the lease therefore does not waive the 90-day requirement.

**The other parts of the clause are lawful:**
- **Once in any 12-month period** matches section 119. No increase is allowed within 12 months of the tenancy starting or of the last increase.
- **Up to the guideline amount** matches section 120. Because the unit has no exemption under section 6.1, the annual guideline cap applies.

So if the landlord gives 90 days' notice in the approved form, a guideline increase once every 12 months is lawful, because the Act itself allows it. The 30-day mechanism in the clause cannot be enforced. A tenant who received only 30 days' notice would not owe the increased rent, since section 116(4) makes such an increase void.

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 116
